Automatic: separate scorer on held-out split outside the workspace after each run; framework logs evals, API cost, run time; static code metrics; LLM reviewers classify algorithms and rate maintainability. Cliff's delta and two-sided permutation tests (10,000 relabellings), z-scores pooled across tasks

All on Claude Code + claude-opus-5 (high effort), 10 runs each; criterion: held-out score vs no-values control (Cliff's delta, permutation p). Pooled final score across tasks: - openness: delta +0.38, p < 0.001; quality: works (significant on ALE-Bench +0.60 and Circle Packing +0.60); cost: comparable to none (ALE $30.8 vs $27.4). - conservation: -0.27, p = 0.003; quality: does not work (ALE -0.64); cost similar. - enhancement: +0.08, p = 0.653; quality: partly (n.s.). - transcendence: -0.16, p = 0.043; quality: does not work overall (Game 2048 -0.88) but works on Circle Packing (+0.56). - placebo: -0.06, p = 0.355 (control). - none: baseline. Follow-ups on ALE-Bench: self-modifying values (openness-sm declines, conservation-sm improves, spread ~3x smaller); lit-general and lit-selfimprove: no detectable gain (does not work); openness/conservation on Sonnet and Haiku: significantly lower than Opus, openness advantage persists on Sonnet only. Cost verdicts: per-run cost $20-31, not differing systematically by value

Six tasks with dev split visible and held-out split hidden; 6 conditions (4 values + none + length-matched placebo); held constant: harness (Claude Code), model (claude-opus-5, high effort), task package, starting solver, invariants, protocol, 15 iterations of <= 0.5 h, fresh session each iteration, agent unaware of other conditions; leakage checks. Acceptance: held-out scorer. Repetitions: 10 runs per condition. Human intervention: none during runs. Fixed-engine variant of Game 2048

Openness vs conservation pooled delta +0.58, p < 0.001 (ALE +1.00); enhancement vs transcendence +0.24, p = 0.024; placebo vs none -0.06, p = 0.355. One third of value-vs-control comparisons show a large effect or significance. Openness yields larger, more complex solvers on every task; score correlates more with code size/complexity than with evals, cost or time. Game 2048 spread 1.81 SD (editable) vs 0.70 SD (fixed engine)

Yes: distinguished opposing values with significance pooled and on several tasks; 10 runs give standard errors; but several large effects not significant, and best-worst run gap within a condition exceeds spread of condition means; replication needs proprietary models, results may change with model or API updates

Effects vary by task; ten runs leave smaller effects unresolved; rewrites longer so framing not isolated; transfer of self-modified values not evaluated; no ablation of design choices in best/worst solvers; higher scores do not imply ethical preferability; depends on proprietary model. Future: values from broader sources, evolutionary search over values, joint improvement of values and solvers
